title: Steven Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC held that Presbytery did not err in finding that the Session had not unlawfully prohibited Hahn from attending worship at CTKPC. It denied the complaint and granted no relief.
first_summary: Hahn challenged Presbytery’s approval of CTKPC Session’s decision to exclude him from worship until he obtained a psychiatric evaluation addressing safety concerns. The SJC denied the complaint, applying BCO 39-3.3 deference and finding no clear error in the lower courts’ credibility and discretionary judgments. It regarded Session’s action as a pastoral safety measure rather than formal discipline, leaving the restriction undisturbed.
summary: Hahn challenged Presbytery’s ruling that CTKPC Session lawfully excluded him from that congregation’s worship until a psychiatric evaluation addressed safety concerns. The SJC denied the complaint. Applying BCO 39-3.3, it found no clear error in the lower courts’ credibility and discretionary judgments, given Session’s familiarity with the people and events. It characterized the restriction as informal pastoral safety guidance, not judicial discipline: it did not bar sacraments, worship elsewhere, or transfer, and attendance could resume upon medical assurance. The conditional local restriction therefore remained undisturbed.
